title: Getting ready
goal: Talk about washing, dressing and getting ready with reflexive verbs.

intro.text: The reflexive `-(Y)n` is for what you do to yourself: *ýuwmak* (to wash something) → *ýuwunmak* (to have a wash); *geýmek* (to put on) → *geýinmek* (to get dressed); *daramak* (to comb) → *daranmak* (to comb your hair).

vocab.en: face (ýüzümi ýuwdum: I washed my face)
to comb (daranmak: to comb your hair)
to be seen, to appear; to seem, to look

exercises.question: How do you say **I had a wash**?

why.1: *Ýuwdum* needs an object: I washed something.
why.2: *Ýuwuldym* would be the passive: **I was washed**, by someone else.

exercises.label: *geýinmek*, present: I'm getting dressed, you're getting dressed…
exercises.explain: *geý-* + *-in* (reflexive), then `-ýAr` and its endings, all front: *-ýär-in, -ýär-siň…*

exercises.en: The children got dressed and went to school.

reject.why: *-il* is the passive: **being put on**. For getting dressed, the reflexive: *geýinip*.

exercises.explain: *geý-* + *-in* (reflexive) + *-ip*: having got dressed. The tense is on *gitdiler*.

exercises.prompt: We're getting ready for the trip.

reject.why: *Taýýarlamak* needs an object: to prepare something. **Get ready** is reflexive: *taýýarlanýarys*.

exercises.explain: *taýýarla-* + *-n* (reflexive) + *-ýar-ys*; *syýahata*, for the trip, in the dative.

accept: She is combing her hair in front of the mirror.
He is combing his hair in front of the mirror.
She combs her hair in front of the mirror.
He combs his hair in front of the mirror.
She is combing her hair at the mirror.
He is combing his hair at the mirror.

exercises.question: In *Nahar taýýarlandy*, is *taýýarlandy* passive or reflexive?
options: reflexive: the meal got itself ready

why.1: A meal can't prepare itself: someone prepared it.

exercises.explain: Same shape, two jobs. In *Biz taýýarlandyk* (we got ready), the form is reflexive; the subject tells you which.

reject.why: *Ýuwunmak* is the whole wash, with no object. For a part of you, use *ýuwmak*: *ýüzüňi ýuw*.

accept: The mountains can be seen from far away.
The mountains are visible from far away.
The mountains [can be seen|are visible] from [afar|a distance|a long way off].
You can see the mountains from far away.

exercises.en: I have a wash in the morning.

reject.why: *-ul* is the passive: **I am washed**. For washing yourself, the reflexive: *ýuwunýaryn*.

exercises.question: Which verb means **to appear, to seem**?

why.1: *Görülmek* is the passive: **to be seen** by someone.
why.2: *Görüşmek* is **to meet, to see each other**.

exercises.explain: *gör-* + *-ün*: the reflexive has become a word of its own, **to appear, to look**.

exercises.prompt: I got dressed quickly and left.
exercises.explain: *geýinip* (having got dressed), then *gitdim*: the tense goes on the last verb.
